title: Firnwell security onboarding discussion
summary: Discovery call focused on Firnwell's security requirements for an LLM inference partner: SOC2/ISO needs, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and audit log expectations, encryption and KMS strategy, data residency and retention policy. Discussed tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and next steps to share SOC2 report, SAML integration guide, and an initial pilot plan.
topics: Encryption at rest / KMS / HSM options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs

SE to share SAML/SCIM integration guide and RBAC examples (Luis) - by 2026-07-10

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07
Start: 3:30 PM PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luis (Redwood SE), Priya (Firnwell Head Platform), Ethan (CTO), Marisol (Security)

Auto-generated summary: brief intake call; privacy and KMS are primary blockers for pilot; leaning toward Dedicated or Private due to data residency and audit requirements.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Maya Chen, Redwood AE. Luis from our SE team is on, and we wanted to run through your security and hosting requirements so we can map to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[00:18] Priya: Hi, thanks, Maya. I'll hand off to Marisol for the security question list, but first quick context: Firnwell wants to push an LLM assistant for internal ops and some customer-facing summaries. Data touches PII and transaction metadata.
[00:35] Marisol: Right, so SOC 2 is table stakes for us. We also have ISO 27001 in scope for our next audit window. We need to know if Redwood can provide SOC2 Type II and which controls are in scope. Also wanting confirmation on retention windows for audit logs.
[00:50] Luis: Totally. We can provide SOC2 Type II reports; our hosted product is under that audit. Quick note—sometimes the export shows Red Wood hosted as the control plane, apologies if the auto text says that, it's "Redwood". For ISO, we have documentation—I'll drop the scope.
[01:08] Ethan: If I can jump in—our legal team will want encryption at rest and BYOK options. We have a vendor-managed KMS today and prefer customer-managed keys for certain datasets. Is HSM-backed KMS available?
[01:24] Luis: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have options for bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with specific entitlements. HSM-backed KMS is supported in Private deployments where the control plane can integrate with your HSM or a partner HSM.
[01:40] Marisol: Okay, good. What about RBAC—do you support fine-grained roles? We need separation between auditors, ops, and developer roles and the ability to grant model-level access.
[01:55] Maya: We have RBAC in the Console: role templates plus custom roles, and token-scoped permissions. I'll let Luis give the tech detail on scoping to model endpoints.
[02:06] Luis: In practice you can scope tokens to per-route or per-model access, and we support role-based mappings from SAML assertions to console roles. Small note: sometimes the SAML mapping docs get transcribed as SAM L or S A M L, sorry for the mess. We support SCIM for user provisioning as well.
[02:24] Priya: Great, SCIM will save us a lot of manual work. Our IdP is Okta but we also have some G Suite accounts. Any gotchas?
[02:33] Luis: Okta is standard, should be straightforward. We'll provide a SAML service provider metadata file and SCIM endpoints. There are occasional attributes mismatch—email vs userPrincipalName—so we'll include mapping examples.
[02:45] Marisol: Audit logs—do you retain raw request/response payloads? We need to know what gets logged and how long persisted logs are kept. Also, can logs be forwarded to our SIEM?
[03:00] Maya: By default we keep metadata-level logs in Hosted for 90 days in the Console. For Dedicated/Private you can configure retention and forwarding. We also support log streaming to customer S3 or syslog / SIEM endpoints. We do not keep persistent customer content in Hosted beyond configured windows unless you opt in for retention for debugging.
[03:20] Marisol: That's helpful. For PCI/PII segments we may want zero-retention for payloads by default. Is there a way to redact or not store request bodies?
[03:31] Luis: Yes, you can disable request body logging or mask fields. Also our prefix KV cache and prompt caching are configurable to avoid storing sensitive payloads. Note: some mitigation requires slightly different batching to remain cost-efficient.
[03:45] Ethan: About deployment modes—what are the main tradeoffs if we choose Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? We're trying to balance engineering ops burden vs compliance.
[03:56] Maya: Hosted is fastest to get started, lower ops burden, but limited BYOK and some advanced network controls. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and more control over keys and log retention; Private gives full control with an on-prem or VPC control plane and HSM integration, but larger procurement and longer lead times.
[04:15] Priya: Do you have typical lead times for Private? Our security team will push back if it's multi-month.
[04:22] Luis: Private deployments typically range 6-10 weeks once contracts and infra are ready; Dedicated can be provisioned in 2-4 weeks depending on capacity. Hosted is immediate. These are rough—I'll include timelines in the doc.
[04:36] Marisol: For SOC2, do you support subservice org model? Our auditors ask that third parties deliver certain controls.
[04:45] Maya: Yes, we provide the SOC2 report and a subservice org letter showing which controls we cover. We'll also provide an artifact list and a contact for auditor rechecks.
[04:56] Priya: On data residency—we have EU workloads and need data to stay in eu-west regions. Does Redwood Hosted allow region pinning?
[05:08] Luis: We support region routing and can pin workloads to region endpoints; for Hosted we have limited region availability depending on capacity zones. Dedicated and Private give you deterministic region placement. For EU-only residency, Dedicated or Private is recommended.
[05:22] Ethan: Any regulatory issues with cross-border logs? If logs are forwarded to our SIEM US region, how do you handle encryption in transit?
[05:31] Luis: We use TLS mutual auth for log forwarding and support AES-GCM on rest endpoints; for cross-border you can choose local SIEM endpoints or route through our VPC peering options.
[05:44] Marisol: Can we do time-limited tokens and rotate keys on a schedule?
[05:49] Luis: Yes, short-lived tokens, session tokens, and automated key rotation are supported. With BYOK you can rotate from your KMS side; we can also schedule automated rotations for service keys.
[06:05] Maya: Quick question—what's your timeline for a pilot? Are you expecting a small POC with some non-PII data first or full production?
[06:15] Priya: Prefer a small POC using synthetic or anonymized data to validate latency and integration. Then expand for internal ops with stricter controls. Ideally start pilot in the next 3 weeks.
[06:26] Maya: Okay, we can scope a 2-week pilot, dedicated model instance on Dedicated capacity or hosted with BYOK and logging disabled for payloads for safety. Luis can outline the exact config.
[06:36] Luis: For the pilot I'd suggest Dedicated reserve with a single model shard to emulate production throughput; we can also do a hosted pilot with strict token scoping if you want faster start. There may be minor perf differences due to our batching and KV cache optimization.
[06:52] Ethan: Any perf benchmarks we can run? We want to validate 95th percentile latency under concurrent users.
[06:59] Luis: Yes, we'll propose a benchmark harness. We'll need a sample traffic profile and sequence lengths. We'll provide tooling to run load tests and capture p95/p99. I'll note that quantization and model variant choices will affect latency.
[07:14] Marisol: On encryption at rest—if we use Hosted with BYOK, where are keys stored, and do you ever have access?
[07:22] Luis: With BYOK, keys are in your cloud KMS and we get short-lived tokens to decrypt for runtime operations; we do not hold long-term access to your plaintext keys. For Private with HSM, keys stay in your HSM and we orchestrate calls without key export. We'll provide diagrams in the security packet.
[07:38] Priya: Can auditors do live inspections or rotate logs on demand?
[07:44] Maya: We have audit hooks and an auditor access process; we can provide export bundles and a contact for auditor requests. We'll avoid sharing customer data—exports are curated and redacted if needed.
[07:56] Ethan: Are there any compliance gaps you know of for financial services specifically?
[08:02] Luis: Our main gap would be if you need SOC 1 or PCI scoped controls—we don't typically hold PCI scope unless specifically contracted. For SOC2 financial controls we provide attestations. We'll include the detailed control matrix.
[08:17] Marisol: About RBAC again—do you have separation of duties for billing vs security? We don't want billing admins to spin up models with sensitive access.
[08:27] Maya: Yes, billing and security can be separate roles; RBAC templates include billing-only, security-auditor, developer, and ops. Custom roles are available too.
[08:38] Luis: A note on tokens—the console issues API tokens and you can pin them to a role with expiration. We also support ephemeral session tokens via your IdP for console sessions.
[08:50] Priya: Great. One last blocker—data deletion requests. If a user asks to delete historical transcripts, how do you handle that?
[08:58] Luis: We have a deletion API and policy. For Hosted we can remove persisted artifacts and purge cache entries; for complete air-gapped removal Private gives you more deterministic control. We'll document SLAs for deletion—commonly 7-30 days depending on backups and retention policies.
[09:14] Marisol: Okay that's important. Also logging access—who in Redwood can see logs? Is there internal RBAC and logging of Redwood operator access?
[09:24] Maya: Yes, we have internal access controls, audit trails for operator actions, and we can provide details in the SOC2 artifacts. All operator access is logged and part of our internal change control.
[09:36] Ethan: Any known outages historically tied to model fallbacks or cross-region failover? We need an SLA for latency and uptime.
[09:45] Luis: We have SLA tiers for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has best-effort with published uptimes; Dedicated/Private can have SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. For failover we support multi-region routing and automated fallback to compatible model variants. We'll include our SLA doc.
[09:59] Priya: How about pen testing—do you allow customer-initiated pen tests against Dedicated or Private endpoints?
[10:07] Maya: We allow coordinated pen tests under NDA, typically for Dedicated and Private. We have a process and point of contact in security operations.
[10:16] Marisol: Can you outline the log schema? We want to be sure sensitive fields are not accidentally included.
[10:23] Luis: We'll share the log schema; by default we log metadata like request id, timestamps, model name, tokens consumed, and anonymized latency. Request/response bodies are optional and maskable.
[10:36] Priya: Ok, sounds good. Can you also clarify the cost differential between Hosted vs Dedicated for a 10k monthly tokens workload and estimated per-token CPU/GPU cost?
[10:47] Maya: I'll follow up with pricing; rough rule: Hosted is usage-based per token, Dedicated is reserved capacity so effective unit cost is lower at scale but requires commit. I'll include an estimated cost model in the follow-up.
[11:01] Ethan: Anything else on legal—data processing addendum, sub-processors list?
[11:08] Maya: Yes we have a DPA and subprocessors list; we'll include the latest versions.
[11:15] Marisol: For the pilot I'd like payload redaction turned on and logs sent to our SIEM with a separate retention window of 180 days for metadata only. Is that doable?
[11:26] Luis: Yes, that's doable on Dedicated. For Hosted we can forward logs but retention windows depend on subscription; we'll propose a pilot config that meets your 180-day metadata retention and zero retention for request bodies.
[11:40] Priya: Perf expectations—if we do Dedicated with a single GPU pool, what's the expected latency range for a 2k token generation?
[11:50] Luis: Depends on model variant and quantization; rough p95 could be 300-600ms for smaller models, up to several seconds for large base models. We'll run targeted benchmarks for your payloads.
[12:05] Maya: Alright, to wrap—action items and next steps, we'll send SOC2, SAML/SCIM guides, propose pilot configs and timelines, and schedule a follow-up to review Marisol's retention policy in detail.
[12:20] Ethan: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[12:24] -- End of recording (note: automatic timestamps may drift)
notes: Slight transcription artifacts present (e.g., "Red Wood" instead of "Redwood", occasional mislabel of SAML). Customer leans Dedicated but will consider Private if auditors require HSM and on-prem keys. Pilot requested within 3 weeks; security requires BYOK/HSM options and log forwarding.
